mainTopic: Which work is allowed on חול המועד: harvesting, work for the מועד's needs, stories of great people held to a higher standard, and the penalty for planning work for the מועד
overview: The amud opens by closing an earlier discussion: some cases are פטור אבל אסור, and some are fully allowed. רב הונא had his field harvested on חול המועד. His son challenged him from a ברייתא that forbids working attached crops unless one has nothing to eat. רב הונא answered that this strict view is רבי יוסי's alone, and the גמרא defends that answer. A ברייתא then allows grinding, cutting wood and brewing beer for the מועד's needs, and leftovers may be used. Whether one may use a trick to make extra is an argument between תנאים. Several stories follow: רב and שמואל, רבי יהודה נשיאה and רבי אמי, רב אשי's forest, רב יהודה's crops, and רבי ינאי's orchard. Some of them teach that an אדם חשוב is held to a stricter standard. The new משנה allows bringing in fruit because of thieves and taking flax out of the soaking pool, but forbids planning work for the מועד. The גמרא explains that the fruit must be brought in quietly, and רבי ירמיה begins asking whether the penalty passes to a man's children. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the earlier discussion: exempt-but-forbidden versus fully permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the earlier cases. Some are פטור אבל אסור, meaning there is no punishment but you should not do them. Others are מותר לכתחילה, allowed from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some of these cases are exempt but still forbidden, and some of them are permitted from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the discussion that came before this section. It sorts the cases into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of 'allowed.' פטור means you are not punished by Torah law, but the act is still forbidden. מותר לכתחילה means you may do it in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden to do
Permitted from the start, with no problem at all

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read פטור as 'allowed.' In the גמרא, פטור often just means no punishment, while the act itself is still forbidden.

phrases.english: Some of them are exempt, but forbidden,
phrases.notes: 'Exempt' here means you would not be punished by Torah law, but you still should not do it.

phrases.english: and some of them are permitted from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The cases fall into two groups: forbidden without punishment, and fully permitted.

steps.title: רב הונא had his crops harvested during חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב הונא had workers harvest his field during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They harvested a harvest for רב הונא during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what רב הונא actually did. This sets up a challenge that is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Harvesting is normally forbidden work on חול המועד. רב הונא clearly had food to eat, so his practice looks surprising. The next step will attack it.

keyTerms.meaning: A harvest; the cutting of grain (Aramaic)
The Festival, here meaning חול המועד (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Rav Huna: they harvested for him
a harvest during the Festival.
phrases.notes: 'The Festival' here means the middle days, חול המועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא חֲצַדוּ לֵיהּ חֲצָדָא בְּמוֹעֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a story about practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא allowed his attached crops to be harvested during חול המועד.

steps.title: His son challenges him from a ברייתא: work is allowed only for the Festival or to prevent loss
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא begins quoting a ברייתא. It allows grinding only for the needs of the Festival, and allows work only for something that would otherwise be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא challenged רב הונא from a ברייתא: One may grind flour on the Festival for the Festival's needs, but not for other needs. Something that will be lost may be worked on during the Festival; something that will not be lost may not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא's son starts a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. Here he lays out its general rules, and the key point comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two reasons that allow work on חול המועד: צורך המועד (needed for the Festival) and דבר האבד (preventing a loss). Anything else is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: For the needs of the Festival
Something that will be lost or ruined if it is not taken care of

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna challenged Rav Huna
One may grind flour on the Festival for the needs of the Festival,
but not for the needs of the Festival, it is forbidden.
Something that will be lost during the Festival:
it is permitted to do it on the Festival,
something that will not be lost during the Festival: forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא לְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins challenging the practice from step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's harvesting on חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Work on חול המועד is allowed only for the Festival's needs or to prevent loss. The decisive limit comes in the next step.

steps.title: The key point of the ברייתא: attached crops are forbidden even if all will be lost
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The loss rule applies only to things already cut. Crops still in the ground are forbidden even if they will all be lost, unless the owner has nothing to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? To things detached from the ground. But crops attached to the ground are forbidden even if all of it will be lost. If a person has nothing to eat, he may reap, bind, thresh, winnow, sort, and grind, as long as he does not thresh with cows.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the son's challenge. The ברייתא forbids harvesting crops that are still growing, and רב הונא did exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the loss rule to תלוש (already detached). For מחובר (still attached), the only exception is a person with nothing to eat. רב הונא had food, so his harvest seems clearly forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In what case is this said?' This phrase narrows a rule.
Detached from the ground (already picked or cut)
Still attached to the ground (still growing)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the surprise: even if ALL the crop will be lost, the ברייתא still forbids cutting it. The loss rule does not apply to crops still growing.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
With things detached from the ground,
but something attached to the ground:
even if all of it will be lost, it is forbidden.
And if he has nothing to eat,
he may reap, bind sheaves, thresh, and winnow,
and sort and grind,
provided that he does not thresh with cows!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמָּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בִּתְלוּשִׁין מִן הַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and gives the decisive point of the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's harvest of attached crops during חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Attached crops may not be harvested even to prevent total loss, unless the owner has nothing to eat. רב הונא had food, so how could he harvest?

steps.title: רב הונא answers: that ברייתא is a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ברייתא reflects one individual's view, and the הלכה does not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is an individual's opinion, and we do not hold like it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his practice. He does not argue with the ברייתא's logic; he says it is a minority view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא calls the ברייתא a יחידאה, the view of one individual. The majority must disagree, so it is not the הלכה. That is why he could harvest to prevent a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual, lone opinion (a minority view)
We do not hold like him; we do not rule that way

phrases.english: He said to him: It is an individual opinion,
and we do not hold like it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in steps 3-4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the source as a minority opinion that is not the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the accepted הלכה, so harvesting attached crops is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a lone opinion, so the הלכה follows the majority, who allow it to prevent loss.

steps.title: Proof: the strict rule is רבי יוסי's view alone
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings another ברייתא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל quotes the same strict rule in the name of רבי יוסי, which shows it belongs to one individual.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said a general rule in the name of רבי יוסי. Something detached from the ground may be worked on even if only part of it will be lost. Something attached to the ground is forbidden even if all of it will be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא backs up his answer. He shows that the strict rule about attached crops comes from רבי יוסי, one single תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same as in the first ברייתא, but here it carries a name: רבי יוסי. Once we know an individual said it, the unnamed ברייתא can be seen as his view. The majority of the חכמים disagree, which supports רב הונא's practice.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not argue with the first one. It says the same thing. The proof is in the name attached to it: once we know רבי יוסי said it, we know it is one person's view.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא harvested attached crops during חול המועד to prevent loss. The ברייתא forbidding this, unless one has nothing to eat, is the lone view of רבי יוסי, and we do not follow it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: an unnamed ברייתא can be matched to one named individual. Once that happens, it no longer counts as the accepted הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated a general rule
in the name of Rabbi Yosei:
Something detached from the ground:
even if only part of it will be lost, it is permitted,
but something attached to the ground:
even if all of it will be lost, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא כְּלָל אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 5 by naming who holds the strict view
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the strict ברייתא is a lone opinion
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל states the same rule in the name of רבי יוסי

steps.title: If it is רבי יוסי, why not thresh with cows?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the strict ברייתא is רבי יוסי's view. That ברייתא forbids threshing with cows, but רבי יוסי does not require changing the way work is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if this ברייתא is רבי יוסי's view, let him thresh even with cows! Didn't רב יצחק בר אבא say: Who is the תנא who requires a change in how work is done on the מועד, even for something that would be lost? It is not רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's answer. Can the strict ברייתא really be רבי יוסי's view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict ברייתא lets a person with nothing to eat thresh, but not with cows. That sounds like a rule that the work must be done in a changed way. But רב יצחק בר אבא taught that רבי יוסי does not require any change for a דבר האבד, so the ברייתא seems not to fit רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: A change: doing the work in an unusual way
Something that will be lost if not taken care of now

phrases.english: But if it is Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: If the strict ברייתא from before really is רבי יוסי's view, as רב הונא said.

phrases.english: let him thresh even with cows?!

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yitzchak bar Abba say:
Who is the tanna who taught a change on the Festival
for something that would be lost?
It is not like Rabbi Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, יָדוּשׁ נָמֵי בְּפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification made in steps 5-6 that the strict ברייתא is רבי יוסי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the strict ברייתא follows רבי יוסי alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids threshing with cows, which looks like requiring a שינוי. רבי יוסי does not require a שינוי for a דבר האבד, so the ברייתא cannot be his.

steps.title: Threshing without cows is not really a change
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי could answer that since people do not always thresh with cows, threshing without them is not a 'change' at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could tell you: Here too, since people do not thresh with cows every day, threshing without them now is also not a change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the idea that the ברייתא is רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on cows is not a demand to work in a changed way. Threshing by other means is normal too, so skipping the cows is not a שינוי. So the ברייתא can still fit רבי יוסי, who does not require a שינוי.

keyTerms.meaning: He could tell you: introduces how the other side would answer

phrases.english: He could tell you:
Here too,
since on every day
people do not thresh with cows,
now too, it is not a change.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: not using cows is not a שינוי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidding cows means the ברייתא requires a שינוי, which רבי יוסי rejects.
steps.terutzMaskana: Threshing without cows is a normal way of threshing, so no שינוי is being required, and the ברייתא can be רבי יוסי's.
steps.whatToRemember: The strict ברייתא can still be רבי יוסי's view. Banning cows is not a demand for a שינוי, because threshing without cows is normal anyway.

steps.title: Grinding and cutting wood for the מועד; leftovers are allowed
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: one may grind flour and cut wood during the מועד for the מועד's needs, but not for other needs. If some is left over, he may use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may grind on the מועד for the needs of the מועד. Not for the needs of the מועד, it is forbidden. If he ground and had some left over, it is permitted. One may cut wood on the מועד for the needs of the מועד. Not for the needs of the מועד, it is forbidden. If he cut and had some left over, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about work done during the מועד for the מועד's needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Work is allowed when it serves the מועד itself. The new point is that leftovers made in good faith may be used even after the מועד. The same rule is given for grinding and for cutting wood.

keyTerms.meaning: For the needs of the מועד

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may grind on the Festival for the needs of the Festival,
but not for the needs of the Festival, it is forbidden.
And if he ground and had some left over,
it is permitted.
One may cut wood on the Festival for the needs of the Festival,
but not for the needs of the Festival, it is forbidden,
and if he cut and had some left over,
it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: טוֹחֲנִין בַּמּוֹעֵד לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹעֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on work done for the מועד's needs, after the רבי יוסי discussion is closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grinding and cutting wood are allowed on חול המועד for the מועד's needs, and any leftover may be used.

steps.title: Brewing beer for the מועד, but no tricks
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on: brewing beer for the מועד is allowed and leftovers are permitted, but only if he does not trick the system.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may brew beer on the מועד for the needs of the מועד. Not for the needs of the מועד, it is forbidden. If he brewed and had some left over, it is permitted, as long as he does not use a trick.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third case, beer, and adds a limit: no tricks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beer follows the same rule as flour and wood. But here the ברייתא adds ובלבד שלא יערים. He may not make extra on purpose, pretending it is for the מועד, just to have some for later.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as, on condition that
He uses a trick to get around the rule

steps.confusionAlert: Leftovers are allowed only when they happened in good faith. Making extra on purpose and calling it 'leftover' is exactly the trick the ברייתא forbids.

phrases.english: One may brew beer on the Festival for the needs of the Festival,
but not for the needs of the Festival, it is forbidden,
and if he brewed and had some left over,
it is permitted,
as long as he does not use a trick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a third case and adds the condition against tricks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Beer may be brewed for the מועד and leftovers used, provided he did not make extra on purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule against tricks shows that the leftover allowance depends on honest intent. It is not a loophole for doing regular work during the מועד.
steps.whatToRemember: Work for the מועד's needs is allowed, and honest leftovers may be used. Deliberately making extra is forbidden.

steps.title: Another teaching allows tricking the system when brewing beer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows a person to use a trick and brew new beer even though he has old beer. This contradicts the earlier ברייתא, which said he may not trick the system.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא sets one source against another: One may brew beer on the מועד for the needs of the מועד, but not for other needs. This is true for date beer and barley beer alike. And even if he has old beer, he may use a trick and drink from the new.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the one from Step 10. That one said 'only if he does not trick the system,' and this one says he may.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that brewing for the מועד is allowed. The clash is only at the end. Here, someone who already has old beer may say 'I want fresh beer' and brew a new batch, even though he does not really need it. That is the very trick the earlier ברייתא forbade.

keyTerms.meaning: And the גמרא pointed out a contradiction to it, setting one source against another
Uses a trick or excuse to get around a rule

phrases.english: And the גמרא raises a contradiction:
One may brew beer on the מועד for the needs of the מועד,
but not for the needs of the מועד, it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֵׁכַר תְּמָרִים, וְאֶחָד שֵׁכַר שְׂעוֹרִים.
phrases.english: both date beer and barley beer.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ יָשָׁן,
phrases.english: And even though he has old beer,
he may use a trick and drink from the new.
phrases.notes: This clashes with the ברייתא in Step 10, which said 'only if he does not trick the system.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second ברייתא against the 'no tricks' clause of Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in Step 10 that one may not trick the system when brewing on the מועד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא forbids the trick and the other explicitly allows it, so they contradict each other.

steps.title: תנאים argue about using tricks
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is explained as a real argument between תנאים. The תנא קמא forbids tricks, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה allows them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is an argument between תנאים, as it was taught: One may not use a trick in this way. רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: One may use a trick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two ברייתות simply follow different opinions. Each one matches a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has to be explained away here. The ברייתא that forbids tricks follows the first opinion, and the one that allows them follows רבי יוסי בר יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is an argument between תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: Whether one may use a trick to do work on the מועד is an argument between תנאים. רבי יוסי בר יהודה allows it.

phrases.english: It is an argument between תנאים.
As it was taught: One may not use a trick in this way.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מַעֲרִימִין.
phrases.english: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: One may use a trick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument between תנאים: each source follows a different opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to be one law that contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different תנאים, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב harvests on חול המועד and שמואל is upset
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב's crop was harvested on חול המועד. שמואל heard about it and was upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: They harvested a crop for רב on חול המועד. שמואל heard and was upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. It is setting up the questions that come next about why שמואל was upset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Harvesting is a big job tied to the field. The question will be whether doing it on the מועד was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle days of the festival (חול המועד)

phrases.english: For רב, they harvested a crop
on חול המועד.
שמואל heard and was upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲצַדוּ לֵיהּ חֲצָדָא בְּחוּלָּא דְמוֹעֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with a story about harvesting on the מועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: רב harvested on חול המועד and שמואל disapproved.

steps.title: Does שמואל follow the lone strict opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's displeasure means he holds like the single strict opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that שמואל holds like the lone individual opinion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether שמואל follows the one strict opinion discussed earlier. That opinion forbids even work that prevents a loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Steps 6-8) the strict rule was shown to belong to one person, רבי יוסי. The הלכה does not usually follow a lone opinion, so it would be surprising if שמואל did.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא tests)

phrases.english: Shall we say שמואל holds like the lone individual opinion?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי יוסי's strict view from Steps 6-8, which only one person held.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind שמואל's reaction in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שמואל's displeasure mean he follows the lone strict view of רבי יוסי?

steps.title: It was wheat, which would not spoil
steps.stepSummary: No. The crop was wheat, which would not have been ruined by waiting, so even the majority opinion forbids harvesting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It was a wheat harvest, which would not have been ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל does not need the strict opinion. Wheat can wait until after the מועד, so there was no loss to prevent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that work on the מועד is allowed to prevent a loss. Wheat standing in the field does not spoil quickly, so there was no loss, and the harvest was forbidden according to everyone.

phrases.english: No, it was a wheat harvest,
which would not have been ruined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wheat does not spoil, so there was no loss to justify harvesting; even the majority would forbid it.

steps.title: Why did רב harvest then?
steps.stepSummary: If wheat would not spoil, why did רב allow the harvest?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, what was his reason for doing this?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the question around. If there was no loss, why did רב harvest at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 made שמואל's anger reasonable. But that leaves רב looking like he did something forbidden, so the גמרא needs to explain his side.

phrases.english: And רב, what is the reason he did this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from Step 15: if wheat would not spoil, רב's action needs a reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What allowed רב to harvest wheat that would not spoil?

steps.title: רב had nothing to eat
steps.stepSummary: רב was in the situation of someone who has nothing to eat, so he could harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was someone who had nothing to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב had no food. A person with nothing to eat may do this work on the מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not about saving the crop. It is about the person's need for food on the מועד itself, which is an allowed reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who has nothing to eat

phrases.english: He was one who had nothing to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב lacked food, so the harvest was for the needs of the מועד.

steps.title: שמואל was not told the full story
steps.stepSummary: If רב was allowed, why was שמואל upset? Because the people who told him did not finish the story.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל? They did not finish the story in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל was upset if רב was allowed, and answers right away. שמואל heard only part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was told about the harvest but not that רב had nothing to eat. With the full facts, he would not have been upset.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not finish the story in front of him

phrases.english: And שמואל, why was he upset?
They did not finish the story in front of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once רב is justified (Step 17), שמואל's anger needs explaining again.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Missing facts: שמואל did not know the whole story.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל disagreed with רב's action itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל would have agreed had he known רב had nothing to eat.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: שמואל knew everything, but he felt an important person like רב should be stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, an important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason for שמואל's displeasure. Even if it was allowed, a leader like רב should have held back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here שמואל knew the full facts. He did not say it was forbidden; he felt that a respected person like רב should have acted more strictly.
steps.whatToRemember: רב harvested because he had no food. שמואל was upset either because he did not hear the whole story or because an important person should be stricter.

phrases.english: Alternatively, an important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question as Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Higher standard for an important person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל must have been missing facts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with the full facts, שמואל expected more care from someone as important as רב.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה's seal ring and heated water
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי יהודה נשיאה went out with a coral seal and drank water heated by a non-Jewish cook. רבי אמי heard and was upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה went out with a coral seal, and drank water heated by a non-Jewish cook. רבי אמי heard and was upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story of a great person being criticized. It sets up רב יוסף's question about what bothered רבי אמי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things happened here: going out wearing the coral seal, and drinking water a non-Jewish cook heated. Either one might be what bothered רבי אמי.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה the נשיא, a grandson of רבי
A coral seal (worn on a ring)

phrases.english: רבי יהודה נשיאה went out
with a coral seal,
and he drank water
that a non-Jewish cook had heated.
רבי אמי heard and was upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה נְפַק בְּחוּמַרְתָּא דִמְדוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, parallel to the story of רב and שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story: רבי אמי was upset that רבי יהודה נשיאה went out with a coral seal and drank water heated by a non-Jew.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks why רבי אמי was upset
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks what the reason was for רבי אמי's displeasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the reason he was upset?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף opens an investigation. He will now look at each of the two actions to see which one was a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there were two actions, רב יוסף needs to check each one. He starts with the seal.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
What is the reason he was upset?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי טַעְמָא אִיקְּפַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the story in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two actions bothered רבי אמי, and why?

steps.title: The seal cannot be the problem
steps.stepSummary: If it was because of the coral seal, a ברייתא teaches that rings are like any utensil that may be carried in a courtyard. So the seal should not be a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of the coral seal, it was taught: bracelets, nose rings and rings are like all utensils that may be carried in a courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tests the first possible reason, the seal, and shows it fails. A ברייתא treats rings like ordinary utensils that may be carried in a courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts jewelry in the same group as other utensils that may be carried in a courtyard. So wearing the seal ring does not seem wrong, and the seal cannot be the reason רבי אמי was upset.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introducing a challenge)
That may be carried in a courtyard

phrases.english: If it is because of the coral seal,
but it was taught:
Bracelets, nose rings and rings
are like all the utensils
that may be carried in a courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם חוּמַרְתָּא דִמְדוּשָׁא, הָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to רב יוסף's question in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the coral seal was the reason for רבי אמי's displeasure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats rings like ordinary utensils that may be carried in a courtyard, so wearing the seal was not a problem.

steps.title: The heated water should not be a problem either
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אמי was upset about the water heated by a non-Jewish cook, that is also hard to understand, because רב taught that food eaten raw is not included in בישולי גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he was upset because רבי יהודה נשיאה drank water heated by a non-Jewish cook, didn't שמואל בר יצחק say in the name of רב: anything that can be eaten raw is not included in the prohibition of food cooked by non-Jews?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second possible reason for רבי אמי's displeasure, the heated water, and shows that it also seems allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water can be drunk as it is, without cooking. רב's rule says anything eaten raw is not affected by בישולי גוים, so heating by a non-Jew changes nothing. Now neither the seal nor the water explains why רבי אמי was upset.

keyTerms.meaning: Food cooked by non-Jews, which חכמים forbade
Eaten as it is, raw, without cooking

phrases.english: And if it was because he drank water
heated by a non-Jewish cook,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: didn't שמואל בר יצחק say that רב said:
anything that is eaten as it is, raw,
is not subject to the prohibition of food cooked by non-Jews!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּאִישְׁתִּי מַיָּא דְּאַחֵים קַפִּילָא אֲרַמָּאָה, הָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 22: after rejecting the seal as the reason, the גמרא now rejects the water as the reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the heated water was the cause of רבי אמי's displeasure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב rules that anything eaten raw is not included in בישולי גוים, and water is drunk raw, so drinking it was allowed.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: Both things were allowed, but an אדם חשוב like רבי יהודה נשיאה should have been stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both questions at once: the seal and the water were technically allowed, but a leader should hold himself to a higher standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not say the law changed. It says רבי אמי expected extra strictness from someone important. This matches the earlier answer about שמואל and רב in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: An important person, a leader others look up to

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the seal or the water were forbidden. They were allowed for everyone; only an important person was expected to be stricter.

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two challenges of steps 22 and 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the person: the act is allowed, but a higher standard applies to a leader
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the seal and the water were allowed, there seemed to be no reason for רבי אמי to be upset.
steps.terutzMaskana: The acts were allowed, yet an אדם חשוב should be stricter, so רבי אמי's displeasure makes sense.
steps.whatToRemember: Something can be fully allowed by law and still be inappropriate for an אדם חשוב, who others learn from.

steps.title: Cutting down a palm tree just for its sawdust
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person may cut down a palm tree on חול המועד even if he only needs its sawdust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חננאל said in the name of רב: A person may cut down a palm tree during the מועד, even though he only needs its sawdust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling about how much work is allowed on חול המועד for a small need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting down a whole tree is a big job, but the only need is a small amount of sawdust, which is useful during the festival. רב still allows it, because there is a real need right now.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.english: רב חננאל said that רב said:
A person may cut down a palm tree during the festival,
even though he does not need it
except for its sawdust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the גמרא moves from the story of רבי יהודה נשיאה to the rules of cutting trees on חול המועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may cut down a palm tree on חול המועד even when only its sawdust is needed.

steps.title: אביי cursed this behavior
steps.stepSummary: אביי strongly disapproved of cutting a whole tree on חול המועד just for sawdust.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי cursed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports אביי's sharp reaction against רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי felt that doing so much work on the festival for such a small need is wrong. He did not just disagree; he cursed someone who acts this way.

keyTerms.meaning: On it, about this ruling or behavior

phrases.english: אביי cursed it.
phrases.notes: He means the act of cutting a whole tree on the festival for such a small need.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A strong reaction against the ruling of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The practice of cutting a whole tree on חול המועד for only its sawdust
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Too much work on the festival for too small a need.

steps.title: רב אשי goes to cut his forest on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי had a forest in שלניא and went to cut it down on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי had a forest in שלניא. He went to cut it down on חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests רב's ruling in real life; this line sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי is acting as if רב's lenient ruling is the הלכה. The next step shows someone questioning him for this.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the middle days of the festival

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה לֵיהּ אִבָּא בִּשְׁלַנְיָיא.
phrases.english: רב אשי had a forest in שלניא.
He went to cut it down on חול המועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי הֲוָה לֵיהּ אִבָּא בִּשְׁלַנְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing someone acting on רב's ruling from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי acted on the lenient view and cut trees on חול המועד.

steps.title: רב שילא challenges רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רב שילא asks רב אשי how he can rely on רב's ruling when אביי cursed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שילא from שלניא said to רב אשי: What are you thinking? Are you relying on what רב חננאל said in the name of רב, that one may cut a palm tree on the מועד even if he only needs its sawdust? But אביי cursed that!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שילא confronts רב אשי, using אביי's curse to question what he is doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שילא assumes the only basis for רב אשי's act is רב's ruling. Since אביי cursed that ruling, he argues רב אשי should not rely on it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is your thinking? What are you relying on?
But look, here is a problem

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שֵׁילָא מִשְּׁלַנְיָיא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: רב שילא from שלניא said to רב אשי:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ, דְּקָאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: What are you thinking? That which רב חננאל said that רב said:
A person may cut down a palm tree during the festival

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא לַנְּסוֹרֶת שֶׁלּוֹ —
phrases.english: even though he only needs its sawdust?
But אביי cursed it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ, דְּקָאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's action from step 27 using אביי's curse from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reliance on רב's lenient ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי cursed the behavior of cutting a tree for so small a need, so one should not act on that ruling.

steps.title: רב אשי politely says he does not agree with אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that he did not hear אביי's view, meaning politely that he does not hold like it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear it, meaning, I do not agree with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends himself by saying, in a respectful way, that he does not follow אביי here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "I did not hear it" is a polite expression, and the גמרא explains that it really means "I do not hold that way." So רב אשי stands by רב's lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not hold that view

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not claiming ignorance. The גמרא itself explains that "I did not hear" is a polite way of saying "I disagree."

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not hear it,
that is to say, I do not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, כְּלוֹמַר, לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי answers רב שילא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the opposing authority: he does not follow אביי's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's curse should stop anyone from relying on רב's ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אשי does not hold like אביי, so he relies on רב.

steps.title: The ax slips and רב אשי stops
steps.stepSummary: The ax head slipped and nearly cut off רב אשי's leg, so he stopped cutting and came back later.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ax slipped and was about to cut off his leg. He left it and came back again.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a near accident, which רב אשי took as a sign to stop cutting on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after he dismissed אביי's curse, the ax nearly cut his leg. רב אשי stopped working and returned only later, showing in practice that he respected אביי's position.
steps.whatToRemember: רב allows cutting a tree on חול המועד for a small need, אביי cursed it, and the story of רב אשי's ax shows that in the end even רב אשי backed away from doing it.

phrases.english: The ax slipped,
and was about to cut off his leg.
He left it and came back again.
phrases.notes: He means רב אשי stopped, and only came back to finish the cutting later, after the מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The outcome of the story: after rejecting אביי's view in step 29, רב אשי nearly gets hurt and stops.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The near accident led רב אשי to stop, giving weight to אביי's curse.

steps.title: רב יהודה allows harvesting flax, hops, and sesame
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה permitted uprooting flax, cutting hops, and uprooting sesame on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה permitted uprooting flax, cutting hops, and uprooting sesame plants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about which crops may be harvested on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Harvesting is normally work, but these crops may be gathered on חול המועד. The next step asks what festival use each one has.

phrases.english: רב יהודה permitted uprooting flax
and cutting hops,
and uprooting sesame plants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling about harvesting crops on חול המועד, related to the cutting of trees above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חול המועד one may uproot flax, cut hops, and uproot sesame.

steps.title: אביי asks what sesame is good for during the festival
steps.stepSummary: אביי understands why flax and hops are useful now, but asks what immediate use sesame has.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Flax makes sense, because it is useful for covering. Hops make sense, because they are useful for beer. But what are sesame plants useful for?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions one part of רב יהודה's ruling: the sesame, which seems to have no use during the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Work on חול המועד is allowed when there is a festival need. Flax and hops have clear uses now, but sesame seems to need a long time before it can be used, so the permission is puzzling.

phrases.english: אביי said to רב יוסף:
It makes sense for flax, which is useful for covering,
hops, which are useful for beer,
but sesame plants, what are they useful for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the sesame part of רב יהודה's ruling in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission to uproot sesame on חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Work on חול המועד needs a festival use; flax and hops have one, but sesame seems to have none.

steps.title: Sesame is useful for its seeds
steps.stepSummary: Sesame plants are useful during the festival because the seeds on them can be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are useful for the seeds that are on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer shows that sesame does have a festival use, so רב יהודה's permission makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though making oil takes a long time, the seeds on the plant can be used right away. So there is a real need during the festival, just like flax and hops.
steps.whatToRemember: Harvesting on חול המועד is allowed when the crop has a use during the festival: flax for covering, hops for beer, and sesame for its seeds.

phrases.english: They are useful for the seeds that are on them.
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is answering אביי here, even though the גמרא doesn't name him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a festival use that was overlooked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sesame seemed to have no use during the festival, so uprooting it should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seeds on the plant can be used right away, so uprooting sesame is a festival need.

steps.title: רבי ינאי harvests his orchard on the festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's orchard became ready to harvest during חול המועד, so he harvested it then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי had an orchard whose fruit became ready during חול המועד, and he harvested it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי ינאי harvesting his orchard on חול המועד. The fruit happened to ripen then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Harvesting was allowed here because the timing was not planned. The fruit ripened on its own during the מועד and would have been lost if left. This sets up what happens the following year.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the in-between days of the festival
Its time arrived (the fruit was ready)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַנַּאי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא פַּרְדֵּיסָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai had a certain orchard
whose time arrived during the intermediate days of the Festival;
phrases.notes: "Its time" means the fruit was ripe and ready to be picked.

phrases.english: he harvested it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי הֲוָה לֵיהּ הָהוּא פַּרְדֵּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of which crops may be picked on חול המועד (steps 31-33) to a story about harvesting an orchard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit that ripens on its own during חול המועד may be harvested then.

steps.title: People copy him, so he gives up the orchard
steps.stepSummary: The next year everyone purposely delayed their harvest until חול המועד, so רבי ינאי made his orchard's fruit הפקר that year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The following year, everyone held off harvesting their orchards until חול המועד. So רבי ינאי declared his orchard ownerless that year.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. People misused רבי ינאי's example, so he gave away his orchard's fruit as ownerless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What רבי ינאי did was allowed, because the timing was an accident. Others copied him on purpose and saved their work for the מועד, which is not allowed. By making his fruit הפקר, he showed that he would not gain from the bad example he had caused.

keyTerms.meaning: They delayed it, held it back

steps.whatToRemember: An action that is allowed can still become a problem if others copy it in a way that is not allowed. רבי ינאי gave up his profit to undo the bad example.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story leads right into the משנה's rule that you may not plan work for the מועד.

phrases.english: The following year, everyone delayed
their orchards until the intermediate days of the Festival.
Rabbi Yannai declared his orchard ownerless
that year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 34 by showing its result.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When others misused his allowed harvest by planning their work for the מועד, רבי ינאי gave up that year's fruit.

steps.title: משנה: work to prevent loss, but not planned work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows bringing in fruit because of thieves and pulling flax from the soaking pool so it is not ruined. This is only allowed if the work was not planned for the מועד. If it was planned, the results are lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may bring in his fruit because of thieves. He may also take his flax out of the soaking pool so that it is not ruined. But this is only if he did not plan his work for the מועד. In all these cases, if they planned their work for the מועד, the results must be lost.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows certain work on חול המועד to prevent a loss, but forbids planning ahead to do work then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows work when something will be lost or stolen if you wait. It adds a limit: you may not leave your work for the מועד on purpose. If you do, you are penalized and lose what you gained.

keyTerms.meaning: The soaking pool where flax is soaked
He plans on purpose (aims) to do it

steps.confusionAlert: "יֹאבֵדוּ" here does not mean the crops will be ruined by nature. It is a penalty: if he planned his work for the מועד, he may not benefit from it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may bring in his fruit
because of thieves,
and he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool
so that it is not ruined,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּין אֶת מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּמּוֹעֵד.
phrases.english: provided that he does not plan his work for the Festival.
And in all of these cases, if they planned their work for the Festival,
they must be lost.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַכְנִיס אָדָם פֵּירוֹתָיו מִפְּנֵי הַגַּנָּבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, which fits well with the רבי ינאי story about planning work for the מועד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work that prevents a loss, like bringing in fruit or pulling out flax, is allowed on חול המועד. It is not allowed if it was planned for the מועד, and a person who planned it loses the results.

steps.title: Bring the fruit in quietly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that the fruit must be brought into the house quietly, not in public view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: provided that he brings them into his house quietly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds a condition to the משנה's permission to bring in fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed bringing in fruit because of thieves. The ברייתא says it must be done quietly, without being seen. This keeps it from looking like ordinary weekday work done in public on the מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא, the start of the גמרא's discussion

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught:
provided that he brings them in discreetly
phrases.notes: "Them" is the fruit from the משנה that he brings in because of thieves.

phrases.english: into his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיַּכְנִיסֵם בְּצִנְעָא לְתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the first case in the משנה (bringing in fruit because of thieves).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit brought in because of thieves on חול המועד must be brought into the house quietly.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings in beams by day
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף had wooden beams and brought them into his house during the daytime on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף had beams, and he brought them in during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רב יוסף bringing beams in during the daytime. This sets up the next move, because it seems to go against the rule of bringing things in quietly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא just said things must be brought in quietly. Bringing beams in by day is very public. So the reader should now expect the גמרא to ask how רב יוסף could do this.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef had beams,
he brought them in during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story that seems to go against the ברייתא's rule in step 37 about bringing things in quietly, and sets up a question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף brought his beams in openly during the day on חול המועד.

steps.title: אביי challenges bringing beams in by day
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף how he could bring his beams in during the day, when the ברייתא says it must be done quietly.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But a ברייתא teaches that he may bring them in only if he does it quietly, into his house!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges what רב יוסף did in the previous step. Bringing beams in openly during the day seems to break the ברייתא's rule of doing it quietly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from Step 37 requires that permitted moving on חול המועד be done בצנעא (privately). Daytime seems like the most public time, so רב יוסף's action looks like it goes against that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Quietly, privately, out of public view

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, the one who brought the beams in.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Provided that he brings them in
discreetly into his house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's action from Step 38 using the ברייתא quoted in Step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's practice of bringing beams into his house during the daytime on חול המועד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires discretion. Daytime is public, so the action seems to contradict the ברייתא.

steps.title: For beams, daytime is the quiet way
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that with heavy beams, moving them at night would actually draw more attention, so daytime counts as discreet.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For these beams, the quiet way is during the day. At night you need extra men and torchbearers, and the whole thing becomes noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself. He explains that for this kind of item, daytime is the quieter choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of בצנעא is not tied to a time of day. It means whatever way draws the least attention. Moving beams at night needs a crowd of workers and torches, which makes a scene, so daytime fulfills the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Torchbearers, people carrying fire to light the way
The matter becomes noisy and noticeable

steps.whatToRemember: "Quietly" (בצנעא) means the way that draws the least attention. For heavy beams, that is daytime, not night.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume בצנעא always means "at night." Here the גמרא shows that night can be the more public option.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Discretion for these beams
is the daytime,
since at night more men are needed,
and torchbearers are needed,
and the matter becomes noticeable.
phrases.notes: Literally "the thing makes noise." He means people would notice and talk about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה צנעא דהני יממא הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by redefining what discretion means for heavy beams.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the term בצנעא according to the practical situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Discretion means doing it at night, when no one sees, so daytime moving breaks the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Discretion means the least noticeable method. For beams, night requires many workers and torches, so daytime is the discreet option.

steps.title: Are the children penalized for their father's planned work?
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה about flax, רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: if a man planned his work for the מועד and then died, is the penalty applied to his children?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool, etc. רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: If someone planned his work for the מועד and then died, what is the law? Do we penalize his children after him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה about flax. רבי ירמיה asks whether the penalty for planning work on the מועד still applies after the planner has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that someone who planned his work for the מועד loses what he produced (Step 36). The question is whether this קנס is personal to the one who did wrong, or whether it is attached to the produce itself, so that his heirs lose it too.

keyTerms.meaning: Soaking pool where flax is soaked to soften it
He asked him (a question of law)
He planned his work (on purpose for the מועד)
That they should penalize (from קְנָס, a rabbinic penalty)

steps.whyThisMatters: It asks whether a rabbinic penalty is aimed at the person or at the item, which decides whether it passes to heirs.

phrases.english: And he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool, etc.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
If one planned his labor for the Festival and died,
what is the law? Should his children be penalized after him?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעי מיניה רבי ירמיה מרבי זירא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of bringing items in quietly and opens a new question on the משנה's penalty for planned work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the penalty for planning work on the מועד carries over to the planner's children after his death.

steps.title: The question starts to expand
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה begins a second part of his question with "if you will say."
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you might say...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי ירמיה is getting ready to add a second part to his question, which continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אם תימצי לומר" means: even if you answer the first question one way, there is still another case to ask about. It builds a second layer on top of the question about the children.

keyTerms.meaning: If you should conclude, or even if you will say. It introduces a follow-up question that depends on how the first one is answered.
You will find, you will conclude

phrases.english: Even if you might say

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a follow-up to רבי ירמיה's question, assuming some answer to the first part.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A further case that depends on how the question about the children is answered. The details continue on the next amud.
